study_identification.author_journal_year: Kim et al., nature mental health, 2024
study_identification.title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

study_characteristics.study_objective: The objective is to map the normative development and aging of the cerebellum across the lifespan using a large dataset, and to use these normative models to quantify individual differences in cerebellar anatomy in several clinical illnesses.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABIDE, ADHD200, AOMIC ID1000, Beijing Enhanced, CAMCAN, CoRR, DLBS, DS000119, DS000202, DS000222, Fcon1000, HBN, HCP, MPI Lemon, NKI-Rockland, OASIS-3, PING, SALD, SLIM, UK Biobank, ADNI, AIBL, DEMGEN, PNC, and TOP)

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer 5.3; fslreorient2std; flirt; ACAPULCO version 0.2.1; SUIT version 3.4

quality_checking_detail.answer: We executed quality control by running the ENIGMA 1 Cerebellum Volumetric Pipeline QC Scripts with Singularity 1 . We utilized the QC pipeline of ACAPULCO 2 as it detects the number of outliers out of 28 regions and address any missegmentations or outliers. As there are thousands of brain scans, we were unable to inspect each one individually but inspected around 5% of the scans manually...We excluded participants if their scans denoted outliers in at least 2 regions and if each scanning-site had fewer than 5 participants.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: All normative models included age and sex as covariates, while controlling for scanning-site-related variability...To account for scanner effects, we treated the scanning site as a fixed effect in our analysis.

modeling_method.answer: Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping

response_variable.answer: Cerebellar morphology was quantified as lobular volumes or voxel-wise gray matter probability values.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model accounts for site effects by treating the scanning site as a fixed effect.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: To account for scanner effects, we treated the scanning site as a fixed effect in our analysis.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model was trained on a training set and evaluated on a test set from the same data pool.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We split our sample of individuals without diagnosis into training and test sets on the basis of on scanning site, sex, and age.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not mention validation on an independent dataset from the same domain.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not mention validation on a dataset from a different domain.

clinical_dataset.answer: ABIDE, ADNI, AIBL, DEMGEN, and TOP

diseases_studied.answer: Alzheimer's Disease (AD); Autism spectrum disorder (ASD); Bipolar Disorder (BD); Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI); Schizophrenia (SZ)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Mann-Whitney U tests, Spearman correlation analyses
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study maps cerebellar anatomy across the lifespan, revealing heterogeneity within clinical illnesses and linking extreme deviations to cognitive scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Our results provide a voxel-wise mapping of cerebellar anatomy across the human lifespan demonstrating the cerebellum’s nuanced role in different clinical illnesses. Notably, individuals with autism spectrum disorder and mild cognitive impairment exhibited increased positive and negative extreme deviations in cerebellar anatomy, while those with schizophrenia and Alzheimer disease showed predominantly negative deviations. Finally, extreme deviations were associated with cognitive scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Lack of detailed behavioral, cognitive, genetic, phenotypic, and medical history information. Low coverage in certain age ranges. Primarily western populations. Cross-sectional data limits examination of drug effects. Imaging challenges in the cerebellum.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study provides a resource for future investigations of the cerebellum. The voxel-wise models can be integrated with any existing or future cerebellar atlas.
